questions.q: What are the real out-of-box state values on a Requested Item (sc_req_item)?
options: New, Assigned, Resolved, Closed
Open, Work in Progress, Closed Complete, Closed Incomplete/Cancelled
Draft, Submitted, Approved, Archived
Pending, Escalated, Breached, Closed
questions.explain: This is the real fulfillment-specific state model carried on sc_req_item, distinct from incident's or change's state model.

questions.q: Which tool is the current standard for building the fulfillment logic that moves a Requested Item through its states?
options: Legacy Workflow only, since Flow Designer cannot touch sc_req_item
A scheduled job with no connection to the catalog item
Flow Designer — the same tool used for multi-stage approval automation
Fulfillment logic cannot be automated in ServiceNow
questions.explain: Flow Designer is ServiceNow's current standard, and approval and fulfillment stages are often built in the same flow.

questions.q: For a catalog item that requires a human to physically rack a server, what is the right fulfillment design?
options: The flow should immediately set the item to Closed Complete the moment it's approved
Human-fulfilled items cannot use Flow Designer at all
The requester should manually change the item's state themselves
The flow should create a task for the fulfiller, wait for them to mark it complete, and only then move the Requested Item to Closed Complete
questions.explain: Work that genuinely requires a person should wait on that person's confirmation before the state advances.

questions.q: For a fully automated access-request flow that calls a REST step to provision an account, what should happen before the flow sets the item to Closed Complete?
options: The flow should wait for and check the REST response for a real success indicator before closing the item
Nothing — sending the REST request is enough to close the item
The flow should always close the item as Closed Incomplete regardless of the response
REST steps cannot be used in fulfillment flows at all
questions.explain: Closing on a sent request rather than a confirmed response risks marking unprovisioned access as done.

questions.q: What is described as the most common real-world fulfillment failure, and what helps catch it?
options: A flow syntax error, caught by the Flow Designer compiler
A requester ordering too many items in one cart, caught by a cart-size limit
A missing catalog item icon, caught by a content review
A Requested Item stalling in Work in Progress indefinitely, caught by pairing the fulfillment flow with the item's SLA so a notification fires before breach
questions.explain: Stalled items — forgotten by a fulfiller or blocked by an unreachable external system — are the typical failure; SLA-driven notifications catch the stall early.
